title: Rousing grace on the first view: enlightenment and stirrings before consent
source_text: XXXIV. Igitur, ex mente Doctorum istorum, Gratia excitans consistit in mentis quadam illuminatione, & piis quibusdam cogitationibus, affectibus & desideriis, in hominum animis, non expectato illorum consensu, immediate a Deo excitatis. Ad quae proinde mens & voluntas hominis physice quidem concurrit, quoniam sunt actus vitales, a facultatibus illis profluentes, sed tamen non libere: quia sunt actus indeliberati, qui mentis consultationem, & electionem voluntatis praeveniunt.
pass_a_gloss: XXXIV. Therefore, in the mind of those Doctors, rousing grace consists in a certain illumination of the mind, and certain pious thoughts, affections and desires, in the souls of men, not waiting for their consent, immediately excited by God. To which therefore the mind and will of man concurs physically indeed, since they are vital acts, flowing from those faculties, but yet not freely: because they are undeliberated acts, which go before the consultation of the mind, and the choice of the will.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXIV. On the view of these doctors, then, rousing grace consists in an enlightening of the mind and in devout thoughts, feelings and desires that God stirs up directly in human souls without waiting for their consent.

The human mind and will do take a physical part in these, since they are living acts that come from those faculties. But they do not take part freely, because these are undeliberate acts, which come before the mind has weighed anything and before the will has chosen.

choices.why: The scholastic pair: grace that rouses and calls, and grace that helps the will to will and to act; kept as in the previous packet.
